agentSession.note: No corpus states an agent session. A Linear record here is an issue with its team, its comments and the people on it; nothing in it says an agent was delegated a piece of work, what it did while it held it, or what machine it ran on, so the whole family is a gap — `agentSession`, `agentSessions`, `agentSessionSandbox`, `agentSessionSshAddress`, `agentActivity`, `agentActivities`, `agentSkill` and `agentSkills`. Backlot states that absence rather than leaving it open: `User.supportsAgentSessions` resolves to `false` and `Comment.agentSession` to null, and `AgentSession` itself is the id-only stub that field and the `@linear/sdk` fragments need in order to validate. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-29, the vendor's `AgentSession` carries 32 fields, five of them deprecated, and the 31 it declares beyond `id` are the `AgentSession.*` entries this file opens with; most are live session state (`status`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `summary`, `plan`, `context`, `sourceMetadata`, `activities`, `pullRequest`, `pullRequests`, `codingHarnessModelLabel`, `codingHarness`), over `AgentSessionStatus`, `AgentActivityConnection`, `PullRequest`, `AgentSessionToPullRequestConnection` and `AgentSessionCodingHarness`, none of which this schema declares.

agentSessionSshAddress.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] SSH address of the current user's running coding sandbox for this agent session." It joins the family whose gap is recorded on `Query.agentSession`, and it carries a note of its own because the 2026-09-09 scheduled run read it as new surface and because its answer is the family's odd one out: measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-11 with a personal API key, `agentSession`, `agentActivity` and `agentSkill` answer an unknown id with an `errors` member (`Entity not found`, `INPUT_ERROR`) and `agentSessionSandbox` with `Access denied` (`FORBIDDEN`). Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-10: it takes one argument, `agentSessionId: String!`, it is not deprecated, and it answers `null` with no `errors` member for an unknown UUID, for a string that is not a UUID, and for the empty string alike — a client reading it cannot tell a session it may not see from one with no sandbox running. Backlot states no session, so every id it could be asked about is one of those; a constant `null` would match that measurement and state nothing.

dependencyPackageMetadata.note: No corpus states it: it answers package-registry data rather than anything a Linear workspace holds. Linear's own description: "Registry metadata (license, publish date, weekly download count) for a batch of dependency package versions, used by the dependency lock file diff preview. Cached across all workspaces since registry data isn't workspace-specific. A package the registry has no data for (or an unsupported ecosystem) is simply omitted from the result rather than erroring. At most 500 packages per request." Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-29: it takes one argument, `packages: [DependencyPackageInput!]!`, each an `ecosystem`, a `name` and a `version`, and answers `[DependencyPackageMetadataResult!]!`, whose five fields are `name`, `version`, `license`, `publishedAt` and `weeklyDownloads`. This schema declares neither type.

integrationJiraSyncHealthCheck.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[INTERNAL] Checks a Jira project for settings that will make Jira reject the changes Linear sends during sync. Reads Jira on every call." It checks a Jira project through one of the workspace's Jira integrations, and Backlot serves no integration: every other `Query` root with `integration` or `Integration` in its name is a gap in this file, `integration`, `integrations`, `integrationJiraProjectStatuses` and `integrationSyncResourceIds` among them. `@linear/sdk` 98.0.0, which the example's lockfile pins, and 99.0.0, npm's latest on 2026-10-25, neither declare nor select it. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-25: it takes four arguments, `bidirectional: Boolean!`, `teamId: String!`, `jiraProjectId: String!` and `integrationId: String!` ("The id of the Jira integration."), and answers `JiraSyncHealthCheckPayload!` ("[INTERNAL] Jira project settings that will make Jira reject the changes Linear sends during sync."), an object of four fields, `findings: [JiraSyncHealthFindingPayload!]!`, `transitionCoverage: String!`, `failedSteps: [String!]!` and `blockedReason: String`. Asked with a personal API key whose owner is a workspace admin, for four `integrationId` values no integration carries (`not-a-real-integration`, the nil UUID, a made-up UUID and the empty string), it answered each with a 200 whose body is `data: null` and an `errors` member, `The Jira sync health check is not available` with `INPUT_ERROR`. The workspace measured answered `integrations` with no nodes, so what the check answers for a Jira integration that exists was not observed. `backlot/graphql/linear.graphql` declares no `JiraSyncHealthCheckPayload`.

notifications.note: No corpus states a notification. The records carry issues, comments, teams and users and nothing that says who was told about what, when they read it, or whether it is snoozed, so the whole family is a gap — `notification`, `notifications`, `inboxNotifications`, `notificationsUnreadCount` and `notificationSubscription(s)`. Serving any one of them commits Backlot to per-viewer inbox state it would have to invent: measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-06, `Notification` is an interface over 13 types (IssueNotification … WelcomeMessageNotification) whose 28 fields are almost all per-viewer event state — `readAt`, `emailedAt`, `snoozedUntilAt`, `unsnoozedAt`, `actor`, `groupingKey`. An empty connection is not a free stand-in either: the workspace measured has no activity beyond its own creation and still answered a `WelcomeMessageNotification` from both roots, with `notificationsUnreadCount: 1`.

oauthApplicationCodingSessionTrustedSour.note: Linear's own description: "Returns the authenticated OAuth application's trusted-source status for Coding Sessions in the workspace. Requires an OAuth access token with the `read` scope." The status it answers "Combines workspace availability with the application's trust setting", in the words of its type's description, and Backlot serves neither: no field of this schema answers whether Coding Sessions are available, and `backlot.acl.Acl.resolve` turns a token into a person, the admin caller or no one, never an application, while `oauthApplication` and `oauthApplications` are gaps in this file as well. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-17: it takes no argument and answers `OAuthApplicationCodingSessionTrustedSource!`, an object of two fields, `enabled: Boolean!` and `disabledReason: CodingSessionsDisabledReason` ("The first reason that enabled is false, or null when enabled is true."), an enum of three values, `CODING_SESSIONS_DISABLED`, `TRUSTED_EXTERNAL_SOURCES_UNAVAILABLE` and `APP_NOT_TRUSTED`. Asked with a personal API key, it answered a 200 whose body is `data: null` and an `errors` member, `Using an unexpected authentication method (apiKey) for an operation` with `FORBIDDEN`. Its answer to an OAuth access token was not measured: the measurement held a personal API key and no OAuth access token. This schema declares neither type.

organizationCodingInferenceKeys.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] Saved workspace inference credentials for Coding Sessions, without their keys." No corpus states one: a Linear record here is an issue, and none of its fields is a credential. It answers for the workspace, whose root `Query.organization` is a gap in this file, as are `Team.codingAgentEnabled` ("[Internal] Whether the team has enabled Coding Sessions.") and `Query.oauthApplicationCodingSessionTrustedSource`. `@linear/sdk` 98.0.0, which the example's lockfile pins, and 99.0.0, npm's latest on 2026-10-23, neither declare nor select it. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-23: it takes no argument and answers `[CodingInferenceKey!]!`, where `CodingInferenceKey` ("[Internal] A saved workspace inference credential, without the key.") is an object of four non-null fields, `harness: String!` ("The coding harness that uses this credential: codex or claude."), `provider: String!` ("The inference provider: openai, anthropic, or amazon-bedrock."), `baseUrl: String!` and `updatedAt: DateTime!`. Asked with a personal API key whose owner is a workspace admin, it answered a 200 whose body is `data: null` and an `errors` member, `Using an unexpected authentication method (apiKey) for an operation` with `FORBIDDEN`. Its answer to any other credential was not measured: the measurement held a personal API key and no other. This schema declares no `CodingInferenceKey`.

originInstallUrl.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] Builds the URL that starts installing Linear's Origin app into a codebase, or reinstalling it to grant new scopes." It joins the family whose gap is recorded on `Query.originInstallation`. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-07: it takes no argument and answers `OriginInstallUrlPayload!`, an object of one field, `installUrl: String!` ("The Origin URL to send the user to in order to install Linear's app."). Asked once, it answered a `https://cursor.com/codebase/apps/install` URL whose query carries `client_id`, `scope`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `summary` and `include_granted_scopes`. This schema does not declare `OriginInstallUrlPayload`.

originInstallation.note: No corpus states an Origin installation. Linear's own description marks the root internal: "[Internal] Describes an Origin installation that started on Origin, for its installer to confirm before connecting." What it describes is the Origin side of an install: the Origin owner Linear's app was installed on, which of that owner's repositories it covers, and whether the current workspace has connected it. A Linear record here is an issue with its team, its comments and the people on it, and nothing in it says the app was installed anywhere, so the three `origin*` roots on `Query` are a gap: this one, `originInstallUrl` and `originPendingInstallations`. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-07: it takes one argument, `installationId: String!` ("The Origin installation id from the install redirect."), and answers `OriginInstallationDetails!`, whose five fields are `installationId`, `ownerSlug`, `ownerType` ("Whether the Origin owner is a `team` or a `user`."), `repositorySelection` ("Whether the installation covers `all` repositories of the owner or only `selected` ones.") and `connectedToWorkspace` ("Whether the installation is already connected to the current workspace, as after a reinstall that updated it."). Asked for three ids no installation carries (`not-a-real-installation`, `12345678` and the nil UUID), it answered each with a 200 whose body is `data: null` and an `errors` member, `Internal server error` with `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` and `userError: false`. This schema does not declare `OriginInstallationDetails`. The same introspection lists three Origin mutations, `integrationOriginConnect`, `integrationOriginConnectInstallation` and `originInstallationCancel`, which this comparison does not read because Backlot declares no `Mutation` type.

originPendingInstallations.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] Lists the Origin installations the current user started on Origin that no workspace has connected yet, matched by the user's email." It joins the family whose gap is recorded on `Query.originInstallation`, and each item is the `OriginInstallationDetails` that root answers. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-07: it takes no argument and answered `[]` for the user the API key belongs to, so a constant empty list would match that answer and state nothing.

projectUpdates.note: No corpus states a project update. A Linear record here is an issue with its team, its comments and the people on it; nothing in it says how a project stood on a given day or who wrote that up, so `ProjectUpdate` is one of the id-only stubs at the top of `backlot/graphql/linear.graphql`: `Project.lastUpdate` and `Comment.projectUpdate` resolve to null, `Reaction.projectUpdate` is never reached because `reactions` is an empty list on every issue and comment, and `Query.projectUpdate`, `Project.projectUpdates` and this root are gaps in this file. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-11 with a personal API key: the vendor's `ProjectUpdate` carries 22 fields, none deprecated, and the 21 beyond `id` are the `ProjectUpdate.*` entries here. The workspace measured has no project and no update, so this root answers an empty connection there.

quotas.note: Linear's own description: "Public resource quotas for the authenticated workspace. These are not subscription limits." No corpus states a workspace's limits: a Linear record here is an issue with its team, its comments and the people on it, and `Query.organization` is a gap in this file as well. Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-10-07: it takes `filter: OrganizationQuotaFilter` ("Filter public workspace quotas by key.", over `key`, `and` and `or`) and `before`, `after`, `first` and `last`, and answers an `OrganizationQuotaConnection!` of `OrganizationQuota` ("A public resource quota for the current workspace."), whose five fields are `id`, `key` ("Stable quota key."), `limit: Float!` ("Effective quota limit, including workspace overrides."), `name` and `description`. The workspace measured answered 27 quotas on one page, each with an `id` equal to its `key`, such as `max-teams` at 1000 and `max-issues-per-team` at 60000. Since each `limit` includes the workspace's own overrides, serving the measured values would present one workspace's limits as every corpus's. This schema declares none of `OrganizationQuotaConnection`, `OrganizationQuota` or `OrganizationQuotaFilter`.

userViewPreferences.note: Per-viewer UI state, which no corpus states. Linear's own description: "The authenticated user's workspace-level view display preferences for a view type. Returns the user-type preferences that are not scoped to a team, project, or other entity. Null if the user has not customized the view." Measured against api.linear.app on 2026-09-10: it takes `viewType: ViewType!`, an enum of 71 values, and answers a `ViewPreferences` whose `preferences` is a `ViewPreferencesValues!` of 248 display settings, 142 of them per-column toggles (`fieldAssignee`, `projectFieldLead`, `initiativeFieldOwner`) and the rest view-wide (`layout`, `issueGrouping`, `showCompletedIssues`). This schema declares none of `ViewType`, `ViewPreferences`, `ViewPreferencesValues` or `CustomView`, whose own `userViewPreferences` and `organizationViewPreferences` answer the same type for a different row — both scoped to that one view, and the second the organization layer this root's description leaves out. The workspace measured answered `null` for each of the five view types tried (`myIssues`, `board`, `triage`, `activeIssues`, `inbox`), which is what the description says an uncustomized view answers, so serving a constant `null` would match today's measurement and state nothing.

agentAutomationEnabled.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] Whether the team has enabled agent automation." `@linear/sdk` 97.1.0 has neither this field nor `Team.codingAgentEnabled` on its generated `Team` type and selects neither in any document it sends, so both are a gap; so is the internal `Team.joinByDefault`, which that type declares and no document selects. No product default is measured to serve in their place: against api.linear.app on 2026-10-09 neither is deprecated, and the one team in the workspace measured answered `true` for both, as did the workspace's `Organization.agentAutomationEnabled` and `Organization.codingAgentEnabled`, which Backlot leaves undeclared with `Query.organization`.

codingAgentEnabled.note: Linear's own description marks it internal: "[Internal] Whether the team has enabled Coding Sessions." It joins the gap recorded on `Team.agentAutomationEnabled`.
